items.title: Membership cancellation is not atomic with Stripe cancellation
items.businessImpact: A remote Stripe failure during cancellation leaves the membership reading 'cancelled' locally while Stripe continues billing the customer's card. Directly matches the client's #1 reported issue.
items.rootCause: change_status() writes local DB status at line 535, then fires do_action('memberistic_membership_status_changed') at line 546. The Stripe cancel listener runs after the local write already committed; on failure it only logs an Activity Repository entry, with no revert and no distinct failure state.
items.recommendedSolution: Introduce cancel_pending/cancel_failed states; attempt remote cancellation before or atomically with the local write; surface failures in a dedicated staff-visible queue instead of only a per-record activity log.
acceptanceCriteria: A simulated Stripe API failure during cancellation leaves the membership in a distinct, staff-visible failure state, never silently 'cancelled'.
The success path is unchanged in behavior.
tests: Manual staging verification with an invalidated Stripe secret key

items.title: Lipsey's second wholesaler account is structurally unreachable
items.businessImpact: Whichever Lipsey's account (firearms or accessories) was configured first is the only one the system can ever sync; the second is silently unreachable, and a blank account_number can cause credential overwrite.
items.rootCause: findByCode() runs 'ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1' on provider_code alone; LipseysProvider::CODE is a single literal shared by both accounts; the upsert dedup match treats a blank account_number as a match key.
items.recommendedSolution: Add an account_number-aware lookup (findByCodeAndAccount); require the import bridge to pass the specific account; add a UNIQUE(provider_code, account_number) index with a non-null sentinel for single-account providers.
dependencies: Data cleanup: confirm/assign distinct account_number values on existing production wholesaler rows before deploying
acceptanceCriteria: Two wholesaler rows with the same provider_code and distinct account numbers resolve independently.
Neither account's import overwrites the other's stored credentials.

items.title: Lipsey's category mapping is configured but never applied to WooCommerce products
items.businessImpact: Every promoted Lipsey's product lands uncategorized in WooCommerce regardless of the configured wc_category_id mapping. Matches the client's 'product categories didn't seem to carry over.'
items.rootCause: wc_category_id is a savable schema column but VendorProductPromoter only reads the category row for markup_percent pricing; it never calls wp_set_object_terms()/set_category_ids().
items.recommendedSolution: Read wc_category_id alongside the existing pricing lookup and assign the WooCommerce product_cat term during promotion.
acceptanceCriteria: A product promoted after configuring its category mapping shows the correct product_cat term in WooCommerce.

items.title: No uniqueness enforcement on memberistic_people.email enables misattached memberships
items.businessImpact: Direct, evidenced mechanism for the client's 'wrong people attached to memberships' report; get_by_email() silently resolves to the most recently created duplicate on every lookup, including waiver stamping.
items.rootCause: email is a plain KEY, not UNIQUE; create() never checks for an existing person by email before inserting; get_by_email() orders by id DESC LIMIT 1.
items.recommendedSolution: Short-term: staff-facing audit report of existing cross-membership email duplicates (G2A-DATA-002). Medium-term: block/warn on duplicate-email creation; consider a conditional unique index after production data cleanup.
dependencies: Production duplicate-email audit before any hard schema constraint
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate-email person creation is flagged/blocked, not silent.
Existing duplicates are enumerated in a report for staff review.

items.title: Booking Engine capability grants only happen on plugin activation, with no upgrade safety net
items.businessImpact: Most probable root cause of 'no calendar for classes on the backend' and plausibly other missing admin-menu items, given the client's confirmed zip-overwrite deploy process never re-fires WordPress activation hooks.
items.rootCause: register_roles_and_caps() is only called from G2AB_Activator::activate(), reachable solely via register_activation_hook, which never fires on a file-overwrite deploy.
items.recommendedSolution: Add a version-comparison check on admin_init/plugins_loaded that re-runs role/capability provisioning idempotently whenever the stored version differs from the running version. Apply the same audit to every other plugin.
acceptanceCriteria: Capabilities are re-granted after a simulated version bump without a manual deactivate/reactivate.
Immediate unblock available with zero code change: deactivate/reactivate the plugin once on production.

items.title: No visitor-facing chatbot implementation exists in this codebase
items.businessImpact: Blocks a confident decision on cancelling Otter Text — the client's stated replacement chatbot cannot be identified, verified, or checklist-tested from source.
items.rootCause: Otter Text was always an externally-injected script never part of this repository, per the theme's own defensive cleanup code comments. Both in-repo AI systems are staff-facing/dashboard tools, not visitor-facing chat. No chat-widget REST route or CORS-enabled visitor endpoint exists anywhere in the repository.
items.recommendedSolution: Live investigation to identify the actual chatbot implementation (view-source, Plugins list, header/footer script injector, GTM); then build and run the 8-point Otter Text retirement acceptance checklist against it.
acceptanceCriteria: The chatbot's technical implementation is identified and named.
An 8-point acceptance checklist is run against it with a PASS/FAIL per item before any Otter Text cancellation.

items.title: No reliable way to confirm what production is actually running
items.businessImpact: Every fix in this audit needs live confirmation before it can be trusted as deployed and effective, not just present in this repository.
items.rootCause: No staging environment, no deploy manifest, and no confirmed clean authenticated read of the live site was available as of the last check on file; in-repo version constants also disagree with each other in at least one case (theme).
items.recommendedSolution: Fix the Bridgistic/WAF blocker or obtain direct wp-admin/SFTP access; generate a dated production manifest of every deployed component's version.
acceptanceCriteria: A dated manifest of every deployed component's version exists and is reconciled against this repository.

items.title: Waiver-import match statistics can overcount actual account stamps
items.businessImpact: An import can report N members matched while some were never actually stamped waiver_status=signed, because the person record didn't exist for that email. Customer account pages can show stale/missing waiver status even though the waiver is correctly archived.
items.rootCause: The import loop increments stats.members_matched whenever a WordPress user email match is found, but stamp_member() silently returns without effect if no Memberistic person record exists for that email, and does not report this back to the caller.
items.recommendedSolution: Have stamp_member() return a success/failure signal; track a distinct 'matched but not stamped' counter; produce an itemized (not aggregate-only) unmatched/unstamped report.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture row with a WP-user match but no person record is reported in a distinct counter, not folded into members_matched.
tests: Import fixture test with a WP-user-only match case

items.title: No restricted content-editor role or content-correction tracking exists
items.businessImpact: Client cannot safely self-serve website content edits without full administrator access, and has no tracked register of outstanding per-page corrections.
items.rootCause: No capability-scoped content-manager role or correction-register artifact found repo-wide; G2A Theme Control is only 472 LOC relative to the ambition of this requirement.
items.recommendedSolution: Build a content_manager role scoped to page content only, plus a correction-register content type with approved/completed/accepted status, plus a recorded editing walkthrough.
acceptanceCriteria: Client successfully edits and republishes a real page correction using the new role, without admin access.
tests: Manual client-led edit using the new role

items.title: Lipsey's product images are hotlinked, never mirrored locally
items.businessImpact: Product photos depend entirely on Lipsey's CDN staying reachable with stable filenames and permissive hotlink referrers; no local fallback exists if any of that fails.
items.rootCause: cdnUrl() constructs a direct lipseyscloud.com URL from the IMAGENAME CSV/API field; no download-and-attach-to-media-library step exists in the promotion path.
items.recommendedSolution: Download the image into the WordPress media library on first promotion (reusing the waiver-PDF-mirroring pattern already proven in this codebase); batch/cron for full-catalog re-syncs.
dependencies: Storage/bandwidth planning for a full catalog re-sync
acceptanceCriteria: Promoted products use a local media attachment as their featured image, with the CDN URL retained only as a fallback.

items.title: Theme version constant disagrees with theme header version
items.businessImpact: Asset cache-busting query strings have not changed across 8+ style.css releases; any cache respecting query-string versioning had no signal to fetch fresh CSS/JS across those releases.
items.rootCause: G2A_VERSION is a hardcoded literal ('1.27.5') independent of the style.css Version header (1.27.13), used directly as the cache-busting version string on every enqueued theme asset.
items.recommendedSolution: Read the version from wp_get_theme()->get('Version') at runtime, or add a build step that keeps both in sync.
acceptanceCriteria: Both version identifiers agree at all times going forward.

items.title: Waiver export/print routes rely on capability check only, not nonce verification
items.businessImpact: Low-severity CSRF-hygiene gap: a logged-in staff member with the waiver capability could be induced via a crafted link to trigger an export/print action.
items.rootCause: print_url() generates a wp_nonce_url() but maybe_handle_export() never calls wp_verify_nonce()/check_admin_referer() — only the capability check gates access.
items.recommendedSolution: Add check_admin_referer()/wp_verify_nonce() alongside the existing capability check.
acceptanceCriteria: A request with a stale or missing nonce is rejected even with a valid capability.

items.title: dashboard-app ESLint configuration is incompatible with the installed ESLint version
items.businessImpact: None functional; lint has been unenforceable with the currently pinned tooling.
items.rootCause: ESLint 10.1.0 requires a flat config (eslint.config.js), which does not exist in the project.
items.recommendedSolution: Add eslint.config.js migrated from the legacy config, or pin ESLint to ^8.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run lint exits 0 or with real, addressed findings, not a config error.

items.title: Build a Customer Identity Reconciliation Tool
items.businessImpact: Client-requested cleanup/dedupe of existing contacts; long-term mitigation for G2A-CRIT-004's duplicate-creation risk.
items.rootCause: No cross-plugin duplicate-detection or merge tooling exists anywhere in the repository.
items.recommendedSolution: Detect-and-flag only tool: normalized email/phone matching, confidence scoring, staff review screen with side-by-side comparison, approve/reject/hold, full audit trail, reversible soft-delete merges, never auto-merge.
dependencies: Extended identity mapping for POS/Formistic/Messageistic customer stores not fully traced this audit pass
acceptanceCriteria: A seeded duplicate is correctly flagged, reviewed, and merged with full audit trail.
A seeded non-duplicate near-match is correctly not auto-merged.

items.title: Build a membership-linking integrity audit report
items.businessImpact: Client-requested detection of people misattached to memberships.
items.rootCause: No report exists for duplicate primary members per membership, seat-count vs. plan-limit mismatches, or waiver-status-vs-archive drift.
items.recommendedSolution: Build a read-only audit report covering these three rule classes as a first pass; wire resolution actions into G2A-DATA-001's review UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Report correctly flags a seeded duplicate-primary-member case and a seeded waiver-status-drift case.

items.title: Build a unified failed-operations queue / health dashboard
items.businessImpact: Staff currently cannot answer basic reliability questions (did the cancellation succeed, did the sync fail) without knowing which component's log to check.
items.rootCause: Good per-component logging exists (Activity Repository, Email Logs Repository, Stripe event-processed tracking, wholesaler sync repositories) but nothing aggregates it into one view.
items.recommendedSolution: Aggregation layer over existing logs, not a replacement logging system; surfaces failed cancellations, failed waiver stamps, failed syncs, webhook event viewer, cron health, production version display.
dependencies: G2A-CRIT-001's new failure states as a first feed
acceptanceCriteria: A failed Stripe cancellation, a failed waiver stamp, and a failed Lipsey's sync all appear in one staff-facing view within minutes of occurring.

items.title: Stand up a staging environment and production deploy manifest
items.businessImpact: Root enabler of most other findings — client currently cannot test before hard-deploying changes to a live business.
items.rootCause: No staging clone, no deploy manifest, deploys are direct zip overwrites to production.
items.recommendedSolution: Stand up a staging clone (hosting-dependent); generate a dated manifest of every deployed component's version on every deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: A code change can be deployed to staging, verified, then promoted to production via a repeatable process.

items.title: Build a sandboxed staff training mode
items.businessImpact: Client-stated: not confident enough to teach employees the range check-in workflow.
items.rootCause: No sandboxed environment exists for onboarding new counter staff without touching real customer records, payments, or messaging.
items.recommendedSolution: A training_mode flag stubbing payment gateway calls and email/SMS sends, seeded fake scenarios covering every case in the counter checklist, per-staff completion tracking.
dependencies: Live counter-workflow walkthrough should happen first so training mode teaches the verified workflow
acceptanceCriteria: A new hire completes every named scenario in training mode with zero real payment/email/SMS side effects, tracked to their staff account.
tests: Automated assertion that training-mode transactions never reach a real gateway

items.title: Build a MembershipGatewayInterface abstraction ahead of any Stripe replacement
items.businessImpact: Blocks any safe merchant-service migration; client wants Stripe replaced with an in-house-manageable processor.
items.rootCause: Stripe integration is direct API calls throughout, with no interface boundary a second gateway could implement.
items.recommendedSolution: Mechanical extraction of Stripe_Service's existing methods behind a MembershipGatewayInterface (createCustomer, createSubscription, retrieveSubscription, cancelSubscription, pauseSubscription, resumeSubscription, updatePaymentMethod, refundPayment, processWebhook, reconcileSubscription, createCustomerPortalSession); no behavior change in this step.
dependencies: A second gateway adapter depends on the client's processor decision (Fortis is best-positioned given existing Booking Engine precedent)
acceptanceCriteria: All existing Memberistic Stripe behavior is unchanged after the refactor.
The concrete gateway class resolves via a setting, not a hardcoded reference.
tests: Full existing Memberistic payment test suite must still pass

items.title: Build a customer segmentation query layer
items.businessImpact: Directly enables the client's requested email/SMS/social growth push during a seasonally slow retail period despite strong range usage.
items.rootCause: The underlying data for every named persona (active/expired member, range-visitor-no-purchase, class attendee, lapsed, etc.) already exists across confirmed tables, but no segmentation query layer exists on top of it.
items.recommendedSolution: Build queryable segment definitions per persona named by the client, exportable for campaign use.
dependencies: Consent-enforcement verification (quiet hours, STOP handling) before send volume increases
acceptanceCriteria: Each named segment can be queried and its member list exported.
tests: Per-segment query accuracy test against seeded data

items.title: Build campaign automation on top of Formistic/Messageistic
items.businessImpact: Converts existing delivery/consent infrastructure investment into the client's actual desired growth outcome.
items.rootCause: Delivery and consent plumbing exists (contacts, newsletter, SMS, consent events); campaign trigger/segmentation logic does not.
items.recommendedSolution: Build the named campaigns (range-visitor-to-retail, lapsed-member recovery, class-attendee-to-repeat, etc.) on top of G2A-GROWTH-001's segments.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one full campaign runs end-to-end with delivery and consent correctly enforced.
tests: Consent-boundary test: a STOP'd/unsubscribed contact never receives a campaign send

items.title: Build a Unified Customer 360 view
items.businessImpact: Advanced-platform target from the audit brief; natural home for reconciliation and segmentation output once the underlying identity model is trustworthy.
items.rootCause: No single view stitches WP user, Memberistic person, WooCommerce customer, waiver, booking, and POS history together.
items.recommendedSolution: Build only after G2A-CRIT-004 and G2A-DATA-001 establish a trustworthy identity model — building this on unreconciled duplicate data would amplify, not reduce, the existing confusion.
acceptanceCriteria: A single staff-facing profile correctly aggregates all of a real, non-duplicate customer's cross-system history.
tests: Aggregation-accuracy test against a known-good seeded customer
